title: What Is Pub/Sub?
sources: AWS, 'What is Pub/Sub Messaging?' (aws.amazon.com/what-is/pub-sub-messaging): publishers send messages to a topic; every subscriber to that topic receives the message (fan-out); publishers do not need to know who uses the information, and new subscribers can be added without changing the publisher

Google Cloud docs, 'Overview of the Pub/Sub service' (docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pubsub-basics): a publisher creates and sends messages to a topic; each subscription to the topic receives a copy of each message; publishers and subscribers are decoupled

IBM docs, 'Publish/subscribe messaging': publishers do not need to know the subscribers; subscribers register interest in topics and receive every message published on them, in contrast to point-to-point queues where each message goes to one consumer

lines.text: Yesterday, one message went to one worker.
But what if five parts of your app need the same news?
lines.caps: BUT *WHAT IF | *FIVE PARTS | OF YOUR *APP | NEED THE *SAME | *NEWS?

lines.text: The creator doesn't message every fan one by one.
and every subscriber gets a copy.
